title: The destroyer that torpedoed the President
caption:
In 1943 a US Navy destroyer accidentally fired a torpedo at the battleship carrying the President. 🇺🇸🚢
A practice run used the battleship as a pretend target and one torpedo was left armed; under radio silence the warning went out by signal lamp, and it was the wrong message.
Who takes the blame: the sailor who left it armed or the officer who ran the drill?
first_comment: Unluckiest ship in the US Navy or the most chaotic crew ever? Pick one ⚓
sources: Naval History and Heritage Command (DANFS) / Naval Historical Center, 'William D. Porter (DD-579)': on 14 November 1943, during drills with USS Iowa as a simulated target while Iowa carried President Roosevelt to the Cairo and Tehran conferences, the destroyer accidentally launched a torpedo

Wikipedia, 'USS Iowa (BB-61)' and 'USS William D. Porter (DD-579)': the warning was first sent by signal lamp with an incorrect message before radio silence was broken; Iowa turned away and the torpedo detonated in her wake; Roosevelt asked to be moved to the rail to watch
